goal: Recover from a failed connector insertion without releasing an earlier cable clip or violating the declared load/time budgets.
primary_question: On unfamiliar cable layouts and mechanical combinations, when does a learned action-outcome selector improve clip-preserving recovery over competent scripted rules and a cable-aware planner at matched experience?
method_status: Candidate not implemented or trained. Its need and benefit must be established rather than assumed.

scope_decision.success: Robot still holds plug; actual tip/base engagement and continuous declared seating dwell achieved before deadline; required open clip stayed captured throughout; boundary-load and raw wrist/plug limits respected; no forbidden state mutation.
scope_decision.endpoint_is_not: Released/latching connection, electrical/optical function, pickup, grasp-slip robustness, or hardware transfer.
scope_decision.retention_gate: Passive SC latch validation remains mandatory for released-connection claims, but is not a dependency of this newly scoped pre-release experiment.
scope_decision.preservation: Old SC retention measurements and all v1 outcomes remain unchanged; new task/endpoint must be versioned and all new arms use it equally.

apparatus.reuse: Pinned AIC UR5e and current SC collision geometry, native MuJoCo adapter and fixed preset robot grasp.
apparatus.proximal_boundary: A fixed strain-relief anchor, instrumented for reaction load. Call it a boundary condition, not a validated prior latched connector.
apparatus.required_relation: One physically escapable open clip. No weld or closed collar that makes the release endpoint impossible. Validate retention and deliberate release using actual cable geometry.
apparatus.fault_object: One shallow smooth post after the clip along cable arclength; keep it in every factorial cell. A caught route must have a robot-driven escape with measured slack and reachability.
apparatus.fixture: A visible fixed board/mount with port, anchor, clip and post in explicit common coordinates. Added collision geometry is a new task version, not a cosmetic retroactive change.
apparatus.parameters: World poses, clip/post geometry, slack and load thresholds require calibration and a frozen executable config before comparison; this file does not pretend those unmeasured values are known.

engineering_starting_points_not_validate.clock_rule: Hold identical torque commands between registered servo ticks; keep policy, noise, observation and reference clocks fixed across physics resolutions. Validate the chosen servo before adopting it.

cable.mass_correction: Existing compiled 24-capsule model is 0.0533333336171 kg, not nominal 0.05 kg. A 50 g target is a prospective task correction; rerun controls/all arms and preserve old results.
cable.spatial_rule: Conserve compiled total mass, rest length, radius, constitutive bending/twist behavior and justified distributed damping across segment counts; do not equate unchanged per-link density/damping with unchanged physics.
cable.root_boundary: Current point connection has free relative rotation; justify it for translational load/clip study, or validate a versioned finite boot-compliance model. No unsupported boot-torque claim.
cable.material: Keep flat=true across layout variations. Record actual model properties, quasi-static force/deflection, settling and representative contact/clip response; mathematical consistency is not hardware material calibration.

engineering_starting_points_not_validate.limits_note: These are development starting points, not hardware damage ratings. Freeze raw wrist, plug, anchor and clip semantics/limits after physical controls and before comparison.

mandatory_engineering_repairs: Separate native physics integration from servo/reference/observation clocks; the old paired robot runs changed servo cadence with dt.

Choose a coherent timestamp and authoritative raw-force stream. Native solve versus diagnostic post-forward forces must remain separate; never call their maximum a native-only measurement. Freeze the rule before the new assay.

Replace hard-coded zero anchor/post loads, True clip/grasp flags and zero forbidden-event counters with real sensing/geometry and instrumented lifecycle guards. Fixed grasp may be a disclosed construction guarantee, never a measured grasp-reliability result.

Record native-rate minimal endpoint ledger: timing, depth/progress, contact witnesses, clip passage, signed force/wrench, loads, dwell, failures, actions and mutation events. Save full states at decision boundaries and failures, plus a dense evaluation subset.
Verify actual clip and anchor force paths with known-load positive controls; report vector/resultant forces and moments separately from sums of contact magnitudes.
Validate analytic cable-length/slack bounds and actual robot release/insertion witness. Count every failed construction/probe; never teleport into a stalled pose.

task_and_learning_gates.gate: Define and freeze the new task before its data are interpreted. All existing numerical evidence stays scoped to v1; no retrospective relabeling.

Nominal held insertion, free/contact sensing, clip retain/release, anchor-load response and no-mutation controls pass. Representative identical-command physics/spatial checks preserve contact/clip outcome and the ranking of tested repairs within preregistered engineering margins.

Observe an active physical failure of the competent first attempt and at least one feasible repair preserving the clip. Show separately that a plausible bad repair can raise distal load or lose the clip. Require more than one layout; a single cinematic case is insufficient.

Screen local condition absent/present crossed with distal catch absent/present. Measure effects and action rankings; visible offsets that are prevented remain prevention. No blind controller or hidden observation may be introduced just to fill a recovery cohort.

Competent cable-aware rules/planning leave reproducible feasible residual failures or a predeclared material cost deficit. If they solve the support, retain that useful baseline and reject the learning-spend premise for this support; do not claim learning is universally unnecessary.

On held-out actions including bad repairs, a learned model predicts consequences/ranks feasible actions better than strong simple/factored alternatives. Action-ranking reversal alone does not establish a joint-model advantage.
Only then test closed-loop control at matched acquisition/tuning/inference budgets and held-out layouts/mechanical combinations. Prediction accuracy alone is not a control contribution.

first_attempt_and_accounting.common_controller: Freeze a competent actual-target alignment/force controller validated on nominal conditions. It may be an existing local assembly routine; explicitly label that retrofit assumption.
first_attempt_and_accounting.handoff: Event-driven persistent physical contact/no progress or distal load/motion stall while the job remains active; never a tuned fixed-duration push. Calibrate witness windows/thresholds from tracking/noise scales.
first_attempt_and_accounting.whole_request_primary: All initial requests under the declared first-attempt plus repair system: initial completions, pre-handoff aborts, invalid initializations, clip losses, timeouts and process failures retained.
first_attempt_and_accounting.conditional_endpoint: Recovery only on the identical active witnessed-failure cohort; physically replay the complete prefix for every arm and verify pairing. Charge each replay.
first_attempt_and_accounting.prevention_check: Evaluate an end-to-end cable-aware rule/planner before claiming the retrofit is preferable to preventing failure. Do not force that planner through a weak prefix and call the result overall superiority.
first_attempt_and_accounting.mutations: Initialization only between jobs. During a job no reset, pose write, reattachment or scripted restoration; actual clip release or modeled grasp failure ends the task.

shared_information_and_actions.inputs: All arms receive the same declared robot state, plug/port pose estimates, cable centerline/history, clip/post geometry and load measurements. Start with full simulated state and exact known robot-model compensation equally; label perception/hardware limitations.
shared_information_and_actions.no_privilege_split: Actor transforms, clamps, query access and probes are part of the interface; extra information or rollouts are never free.
shared_information_and_actions.repair_library: Small shared set of physically validated parameterized macros: unload/retract-realign, and a clip-preserving cable-clearance arc followed by the same insertion controller. Expand only for a measured failure, not architectural appearance.
shared_information_and_actions.authority: All methods have identical translation/orientation authority, limits and macro horizon. Exclude fault axes the action interface cannot correct.

arms: actual-target force-guided retry with precontact bias compensation
same insertion plus visible cable/clip-aware repair rules
compact geometric/cable-aware planner using the same information and insertion controller
comparison_stages.purpose: Establish a residual problem worth learning; continued straight insertion is a negative control only.

arms: separate local and distal predictors with the same full inputs/history and constrained action selector
small action-conditioned outcome model over the shared repair library
comparison_stages.purpose: Identify what joint prediction adds beyond separate consequence estimates. Freeze target, loss, selector and capacity/tuning accounting.

arms: best learned outcome model plus the same action selector
mechanism-removal ablation retaining inputs, primitives and comparable capacity
comparison_stages.purpose: Determine whether learned consequences improve actual clip-preserving completion and justify their costs.

learning_design.initial_candidate: A compact macro-action outcome predictor/ranker with progress, clip-loss risk and load consequences. No graph, transformer, long-horizon RL or special architecture is mandatory.
learning_design.joint_definition_required: Before model training, state whether the proposed mechanism is cross-conditioned dynamics, shared representation, multi-step composition or correlated outcome risk. A factorial interaction does not uniquely establish any of these.
learning_design.budget: Shared training acquisitions may be reused by each arm, but credit the full equivalent acquisition budget to each method. Charge fault generation, alternate-action prefix replays, failed probes, inference and tuning; report project-total collection once.
learning_design.starts: Target at least three independent acquisition/training starts for comparative claims. Three optimizer seeds on one shared dataset are a weaker result and must be labelled as such.
learning_design.checkpoint_rule: Freeze acquisition and optimizer-update budgets and select by them; no final-test checkpoint selection.
learning_design.hardware_policy: No hardware access invented or required to begin this simulation study. Hardware/calibration is required before claiming actual deployment, retention strength or transfer.
prediction_metrics: Feasible action ranking/regret on held-out good and bad repairs
Calibrated clip-loss or task-completion risk where probabilistic predictions are meaningful
Closed-loop completion and time benefits, separately from prediction error

splits_and_evaluation.freeze_before_use: Save explicit disjoint development/training/test manifests before corresponding runs. Test layouts and mechanical combinations are held out as groups, not merely neighbouring timesteps or repeat seeds.
splits_and_evaluation.seed_note: These are prospective disjoint ranges, not executed random trials. Seed labels must actually drive recorded RNG; deterministic cases must be labelled deterministic.
report: Whole-request unfinished tasks, nominal and fault-cell completion
Conditional post-witness recovery on common support
Time per request including all failures; repair time separately
Native simulator work, wall time, memory and inference/tuning expense
splits_and_evaluation.analysis: Use paired case effects and uncertainty that respects layout/mechanical clusters and training starts. Consecutive frames are not independent trials. Small development screens remain exploratory.
splits_and_evaluation.practical_effect: Declare the minimum useful completion/time improvement and sample size before final tests, using development variance and actual compute. No result is guaranteed; never choose the margin after seeing test outcomes.
splits_and_evaluation.transfer: No unseen-connector claim unless connector geometry itself is withheld; varied cable layouts alone do not establish that.

next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.first_block: Implement and execute the task/clock/guard/physical-support work decisively. Use an initial 32-request tranche for rapid feedback, then expand toward 64-128 meaningful diagnostic requests and relevant numerical/clip controls. These are planning targets, not stop caps. Continue targeted fixes while they make measurable progress; do not abandon a tractable problem after an arbitrary two rounds.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.first_screen: Start with 16 contexts to debug the matrix, then expand to 64-128 registered development contexts across multiple layout/mechanical families. Compare at least the strong insertion/rules baseline and a cable-aware planner before deciding whether a residual learning problem exists. All feasibility and denominator rules remain.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.resource_rule: One serial GPU/simulator queue. Profile corrected native task with rendering off, including initialization and logging. Start small CPU batches/process counts only after parity checks; do not extrapolate old peg 2,048-environment results.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.current_capacity_inference: Existing baseline 721159 native steps  / 405.375 s is about 1779 steps/s. At 4000 Hz physics and 50 Hz policy this is 22.2 equivalent policy intervals/s: 1M intervals about 12.5 h before optimizer/evaluation. This is an extrapolation, not a training capacity measurement.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.gpu_port_rule: A backend accepting XML does not prove that cable plugin forces work. Any MJX/Warp/Isaac port requires positive force/deformation/contact checks and source pinning before adopting it; do not spend the session porting merely to request 2,048/4,096 environments.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.stop: Continue through the complete feasible campaign. If simple methods solve the small starter grid, test a broader practically justified distribution before rejecting learning spend; never manufacture hidden-information or impossible faults. If the broad strong baseline already suffices, complete and release that convincing negative/engineering result. If a physical gate remains invalid, resolve or specifically redesign it instead of burning training compute. Time exhaustion is an incomplete handoff, not evidence of success.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.runtime_work: Treat runtime engineering as part of the campaign: profile physics, control, contact queries, rolling-window bookkeeping, logging and model construction. Separate cadence, remove redundant work only with parity checks, reuse compiled scenes across legitimate between-job initialization, and benchmark small native CPU worker/batch counts such as 1/4/8 before scaling further.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.data_campaign: If physical and residual-problem gates pass, target 1000-3000 physical attempt/repair acquisitions per independent acquisition/training start, including alternate feasible and bad repairs. Derive the actual count from measured throughput, model needs and held-out evaluation reserve; freeze counts before acquisition. Do not mistake these planning targets for measured capacity.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.training_campaign: Target at least 3 independent acquisition/training starts for the selected candidate and relevant learned comparator/ablation. Run sufficient declared optimization to assess learning and reload checkpoints; do not stop at a few epochs because a file was saved. Same-dataset optimizer repeats are explicitly weaker evidence.
next_session_budget_and_stop_rules.evaluation_campaign: Target at least 128 held-out layout/mechanical contexts per training start for the learning comparison when throughput permits, plus matched strong scripted/planned references. Predeclare power/practical margins and group-aware analysis before opening tests. Scale intelligently from measured capacity, not from convenient test outcomes.

demonstrator.required: Overview showing mounted port, boundary, required clip and snag; labelled connector close-up; common-case nominal/stall/repair/held-seat timeline; one success and one failure; cable/clip state and real load trace.
demonstrator.labels: Simulation; actual controller; trained versus scripted actions; playback speed; held terminal frame; endpoint scope. No staged movie or hand-set recovery state substitutes for a physical witness.

handover_rule: Read the active ROADMAP action, implement and execute the bounded witness block; do not restart broad literature brainstorming, the rejected peg prefix campaign, or a universal latch-development prerequisite.

execution_mandate.owner_steering: Be ambitious with the next session in terms of work; do not be conservative.
execution_mandate.objective: Own a full research campaign: implement the constrained task and measurement fixes, validate physical recovery, establish strong baselines, collect substantial data, train justified methods, perform held-out action and closed-loop evaluation, and release the result/demo.
execution_mandate.persistence: Small probes are the first tranche, not the session deliverable. Resolve ordinary implementation obstacles, revise the method when evidence requires it and continue across context compaction. Do not end at a task skeleton, literature review, tiny smoke run or saved pilot weights.
execution_mandate.scientific_boundary: Ambition increases implementation, data and evaluation work, not unsupported claims. Learning still needs a real feasible deficit; a broad, registered negative result is acceptable.

test_access_rule: Use development-only held-out groups for G5 mechanism selection and tuning. Keep final-test groups and outcomes closed until methods, budgets, selection rules and analysis are frozen. Repeated final-test-guided method changes require a new untouched test registration; preserve earlier results.
